purpose: Instructions for creating and maintaining DSA problem pages in the Notion DSA Problems database.
source_of_truth: This file is the authoritative structure for Notion DSA pages. Existing good pages may be used as visual references, but this spec overrides older mistakes.

database.name: DSA Problems
rules: Do not repeat Problem URL or GitHub URL inside the page body because they already exist as database properties.
Create the full solution note directly inside the database row/page.
Use only valid existing Study Patterns unless the database schema is intentionally updated.

pre_creation_checks: Check whether the problem already exists in the DSA Problems database.
Open 1-2 correctly formatted existing DSA pages as references.
Read all provided GitHub solution files for the problem.
Identify whether other meaningful standard approaches exist.
Do not blindly copy old formatting errors from reference pages.

solution_selection_rules.provided_solution: Always preserve and include any solution already provided in the GitHub repo.
solution_selection_rules.other_solutions: Include other standard, better, or optimal approaches when they add educational or interview value.
solution_selection_rules.labeling: Do not assume the provided solution is optimal. Label each approach by what it actually is.
solution_selection_rules.progression_rule: Use Brute -> Better -> Optimal when meaningful, but do not invent artificial approaches just to force three sections.

page_structure.heading: Problem
page_structure.content: Short faithful explanation of the problem.

rules: Use a good non-trivial example that exposes the important behavior of the algorithm.
Prefer examples that demonstrate edge cases, state changes, or the key invariant.
Use visual tables/boxes for arrays, pointers, hash maps, stacks, queues, and trees when helpful.
Do not use trivial one-element examples unless the problem specifically requires them.

notion_table_rule.required: Use real Notion table syntax, never escaped table text.

style.explanation_depth: Detailed enough for revision but not unnecessarily verbose.
code_source_priority: Use canonical/optimal solution as final approach when appropriate

post_creation_checks: Verify tables render as actual Notion tables.
Verify the dry run uses a strong example.
